context.why: A working prototype of the whole Contributors tab is already on this branch and was approved by the maintainer on the running pages. Its templates and components stay exactly as they are; the Python behind them (fairdm/contrib/contributors/access.py, plugins/shared.py and the seed) has no tests and is being rebuilt story by story. This story rebuilds the base: the stored level on a contribution, the RecordAccess class that reads it, the Crediting class that changes contributors, and the tab's list, add-from-the-portal, edit-roles and remove pages over them. Later stories own the rest, and until they land the prototype's code for those parts keeps the pages working: the affiliation choice (US2), the ORCID, ROR and by-hand ways of adding (US3), the permission backend, enforcement on private records, levels on the edit page, the creator's level and the data migration (US4), the last-manager rule (US5), moving and order (US6). Do not delete prototype behaviour another story owns; leave it working and untested.

prior_decisions: decisions.md D5: RecordAccess(record) and Crediting(record) are classes with no base class. D7: a superuser cannot be saved as a contributor (Contribution.save raises ValueError outside DEBUG); Crediting.add refuses one with a ValidationError (give it a code) that the add page shows, never an unhandled exception.

Levels in this story are read from Contribution.level only. Stored django-guardian rows still work for everything else in the portal until US4 switches the backend, so do not touch any permission backend, AUTHENTICATION_BACKENDS, visible_to, or the create pages' assign_perm calls. RecordAccess.can_manage(user) is: level MANAGE on the record or a record above it, or the user holds change_<model> for the whole portal (user.has_perm('<app>.change_<model>') with no object), which is what a superuser and a Data Curator pass.

ContributionLevel goes in fairdm/contrib/contributors/choices.py as an IntegerChoices: VIEW=1, EDIT=2, MANAGE=3. Contribution.level is nullable, empty for an organization, with verbose_name and help_text. Write the schema migration with makemigrations and apply it to the dev server's database (see environment).

The prototype's access.py reads levels from guardian rows through get_user_perms. Replace that module wholesale with RecordAccess on the field. plugins/shared.py imports its old function names in many places, including code other stories own: update every call site so every page still renders. The templates read context names (entry.own, entry.above, entry.effective, entry.label, entry.from_above, entry.has_account, entry.is_person, entry.contributor, entry.contribution, entry.attached, entry.removable, entry.affiliation, people.rows, people.total, people.movable, organizations.*, access_from_above, parent, parent_url, parent_kind, kind, list_url, can_manage, term, total, adding.*), so keep those names.

'Can sign in' is one method on Person: active, and claimed or has signed in (last_login is not None). Specification 020 settled that rule in Person.is_editable_by; move the rule into the method and have is_editable_by use it. tests for is_editable_by already exist and must still pass unchanged.
The tab opens to anyone in this story. Refusing strangers on a private record's tab is US4 (T017 TestPrivateRecordTab); do not build it here.
A visitor asking for a changing page is redirected to sign in; a signed-in person who cannot manage the record gets 403; nothing is changed in either case.

Two pre-existing tests pin the old tab and currently fail; bring them up to date in T004 and name them in progress.md: tests/test_contrib/test_plugins/test_registration.py::TestExtraViews::test_the_shipped_contribution_views_address_their_target (the tab's additional views are now add-person, add-organization, edit, remove and move) and tests/test_core/test_dataset/test_plugins.py::TestRetiredManagementPages::test_the_dataset_menu_carries_one_entry (a dataset now also carries the Contributors tab). Keep what each test is for; change only the expectation the new tab alters.

The seeds (demo/seed/contributors.py, demo/seed/common.py grant_team_rights, demo/seed/projects.py) currently give rights with guardian rows. In this story demo/seed/contributors.py sets levels through Crediting. demo/seed/common.py and demo/seed/projects.py must keep working for the existing overview pages until US4, so in this story make them ALSO set the level (through Crediting) while still granting the rows; US4 removes the rows. Do not rerun seed_contributors without --keep-records against the dev database: the maintainer has the record addresses.

After your migration, the seeded dev database has contributions with no level. Set them once so the running pages still show the right thing: for the records seed_contributors made, give each person the level their guardian rows amount to (view/change/delete on the record means view/edit/manage). Do it with a one-off shell snippet, not a migration (the real conversion is US4's data migration), and say in your report that you did.

Documentation (T005): the docs gate fails today on 17 public names the prototype added and no page mentions. Your pages must cover the names this story leaves public. Names belonging to later stories' code will keep the docs step red until their stories; list in your report which undocumented names remain and which story owns each.
